encapsulation-and-validation.label: Encapsulation and Validation
encapsulation-and-validation.summary: Protect object state by validating state-changing methods, then use a property setter when direct attribute assignment also needs one controlled validation path.

sketch1.title: Protect direct assignment with a property

try_encapsulation_and_validation_sketch0.title: Protect mileage inside drive()
try_encapsulation_and_validation_sketch0.prompt: `main.py` is already complete. In `models/car.py`, update the existing `drive(self, miles)` method so it changes `self.miles` only when the requested `miles` value is greater than `0`. For zero or a negative value, leave the stored mileage unchanged. Always return the car's current mileage. Leave `main.py` unchanged.
try_encapsulation_and_validation_sketch0.hint: Check the requested distance before mutating `self.miles`, then return the current mileage.

help.concept: Validation belongs next to the state change it protects. Invalid requests should not mutate the object.
help.hint_2: Return the current mileage after the validation decision.

try_encapsulation_and_validation_sketch1.title: Validate direct mileage assignment
try_encapsulation_and_validation_sketch1.prompt: `main.py` is already complete. In `models/car.py`, keep `_miles` as the backing attribute and add a `miles` property. The `@property` getter `miles(self)` must return the backing mileage. Add a `@miles.setter` setter that changes the backing mileage only when the new value is `0` or greater. Negative assignments must leave the current mileage unchanged. Keep `__init__` routing the starting value through `self.miles = miles`. Leave `main.py` unchanged.
try_encapsulation_and_validation_sketch1.hint: The getter exposes the backing value. The setter validates before replacing that value.

help.concept: A property preserves normal attribute syntax while giving the object one controlled validation path.
help.hint_1: Use `@property` for the getter and `@miles.setter` for the setter.

mc-encapsulation-and-validation-safe-des.title: Choose controlled state changes
mc-encapsulation-and-validation-safe-des.prompt: Which designs keep validation close to the state it protects? Choose all that apply.
mc-encapsulation-and-validation-safe-des.hint: Look for one controlled path that every caller uses.

help.concept: State-changing methods and property setters can both keep a validation rule inside the object.
help.hint_1: A method can validate before mutation.
help.hint_2: A property setter can validate direct assignment.

options.a: `drive()` checks a distance before changing the car's mileage.
options.b: `main.py` directly repairs `_miles` whenever a value looks wrong.
options.c: A `miles` property setter validates `car.miles = value` assignments.
options.d: Every caller invents its own validation rule before touching the object.

sc-encapsulation-and-validation-why-insi.title: Why use a property setter?
sc-encapsulation-and-validation-why-insi.prompt: Why is a property setter useful for a value such as `miles`?
sc-encapsulation-and-validation-why-insi.hint: Think about normal assignment syntax plus validation.

help.concept: A property setter lets callers assign normally while the object controls whether the new value is accepted.
help.hint_1: The caller can still write `car.miles = value`.
help.hint_2: The setter owns the validation rule.

options.a: It prevents callers from reading the attribute at all.
options.b: It keeps normal assignment syntax while validating the new value inside the object.
options.c: It makes every instance share one mileage value.
options.d: It removes the need for an initializer.

fb-encapsulation-and-validation-conditio.title: Trace a rejected assignment
fb-encapsulation-and-validation-conditio.prompt: A car currently has `miles = 150`. Its property setter ignores negative values. After `car.miles = -20`, what is `car.miles`?
fb-encapsulation-and-validation-conditio.hint: A rejected assignment leaves the stored state unchanged.

help.concept: Validation protects the existing object state when an assignment is invalid.

sketch-0.title: Reject invalid changes before mutating state
sketch-0.bodyMarkdown:
A state-changing method should reject changes that would make the object invalid.

```python
class Wallet:
    def withdraw(self, amount):
        if amount <= 0 or amount > self.balance:
            return False

        self.balance -= amount
        return True
```

The method protects the Wallet's state instead of trusting every caller to repeat the validation correctly.

A rejected operation should leave the stored state unchanged.
